answer: Vote weight sits in a kernel ledger decaying 10% each epoch unless its owner adds 20 fresh credits. An attacker with 1,000 fake identities must pay 20,000 credits at the wharf desk each epoch to hold weight flat; the k-th fake costs the same 20 as the first, so ten epochs burn 200,000 credits. A rented-vote ring fails: each top-up binds to one kernel key, cannot be replayed, and reused receipts are rejected. A jetty checkpoint at epoch close publishes weights; auditors re-add them, and shortfalls lose rewards. An honest agent adds one 20-credit stake and keeps full weight.
